question: How many ICC World Cups has India won in ODI?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India has won the ICC World Cup in ODI format **twice**.
 
• The first win was in **1983** under the captaincy of **Kapil Dev**.
 
• The second win was in **2011** under the captaincy of **Mahendra Singh Dhoni**.
 
• India is one of the few countries to have won the World Cup multiple times.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ICC World Cup**

 
 
• The ICC Cricket World Cup is the international championship of One Day International (ODI) cricket.
 
• It is organized by the sport's governing body, the International Cricket Council (ICC), every four years.
 
• The tournament is one of the world's most viewed sporting events and is considered the "flagship event of the international cricket calendar" by the ICC.
 
• The first World Cup was held in England in 1975.
 
 
 
• **1983 ICC World Cup**
 
 
• The 1983 Cricket World Cup (officially the Prudential Cup '83) was the third edition of the Cricket World Cup tournament.
 
• The tournament was won by India, who defeated the West Indies in the final to win their first World Cup title.
 
• The final was held at Lord's in London on 25 June 1983.
 
 
 
• **2011 ICC World Cup**
 
 
• The 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup was the tenth Cricket World Cup.
 
• It was co-hosted by India, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh.
 
• India won the tournament, defeating Sri Lanka by 6 wickets in the final in Mumbai.
 
• India became the first country to win the Cricket World Cup on home soil.
 
 
 
• **Mahendra Singh Dhoni**
 
 
• Mahendra Singh Dhoni, commonly known as MS Dhoni, is an Indian cricketer and former captain of the Indian national team.
 
• He is widely regarded as one of the greatest cricket captains and wicket-keeper batsmen in the history of the game.
 
• Under his captaincy, India won the 2007 ICC World Twenty20, the 2010 and 2016 Asia Cups, the 2011 ICC Cricket World Cup, and the 2013 ICC Champions Trophy.
